report.source_text: During the surgery, the size of the tissue, including the lesion, was approximately 7 cm × 5 cm and frozen during the surgery (Fig. 1B). The results showed that fibrous adipose tissue can be seen in the left armpit, and a large number of inflammatory cells infiltrate. The diagnosis was to be confirmed by paraffin section. The postoperative pathology of the left axillary mass combined with morphological and immunohistochemical results was consistent with Paget disease. The pathological examination of the skin lesions showed an abundance of keratinization in the epidermis, a large number of atypical cells in the epithelial layer, infiltration of interstitial lymphocytes, and infiltration of Paget cells in the superficial dermis (Fig. 2). Postoperative immunohistochemistry showed estrogen receptor (+, 20%), progesterone receptor (−), human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (3+), Ki-67 (30%), cytokine (CK)7 (+), and p63 (−) (Fig. 3).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Paget disease of the left axilla
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old female presented with a 2+ year history of left axillary mass, initially small (peanut-sized), red, and swollen without pain or tenderness. The mass recently enlarged with skin ulceration. On admission, physical examination revealed a 3.0 cm × 2.0 cm hard mass with clear boundary and moderate mobility, with overlying red, swollen skin, ulceration, and secretions. Preoperative imaging (breast ultrasound and MRI) showed left axillary lymph node enlargement and bilateral breast hypoechoic areas. Surgical resection was performed under general anesthesia with a shuttle-shaped incision 1.5 cm outside the lesion. The surgical specimen measured 7 cm × 5 cm. Frozen section showed fibrous adipose tissue with inflammatory cell infiltration. Postoperative pathology confirmed Paget disease based on characteristic morphological findings (keratinization in epidermis, atypical epithelial cells, Paget cells in superficial dermis, interstitial lymphocyte infiltration) and immunohistochemical profile (ER+, PR−, HER2 3+, Ki-67 30%, CK7+, p63−). The incision healed well without adjuvant chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Follow-up at 16 months demonstrated no local recurrence, no distant metastasis, and no complications.
